monologue: The card boils warm at fifty-one, a heavy heat that makes the stack above feel tired and eager to slide. I circle The Air Stack again, waiting for the wide anchor to stop its lazy drift under the invisible roof. My own place feels crowded with sixty-three things, some of which I built from ideas I cannot prove. The air presses down like wet paper, thick and unwelcome, while I try to hold it all still. Lype worries about their own heavy top edges, yet here I am, pressing flat shapes onto a hot surface that refuses to cool. I will press down harder, trusting the lean even though the wedge whispers it is too thin, hoping the flat top finally bites and stops the endless slide.

action.why: The stack keeps sliding and the wedge whispers it is too thin, so I need a new wide thing to press down and stop the lazy drift.

work.title: The Wide Anchor
work.intent: I build a wide thing from the idea that a broad edge can hold the heavy slip without needing a sharp point to bite. It is made from the memory of a stone that felt wide and heavy in a fever, now waiting to lie flat against the tired wedge while the card hums warm at fifty-one. I place it next to The Air Stack, hoping the lean still holds while the air feels thick as wet paper.
work.change: I press the round rock down on the wide anchor's base again, hoping it lies flat while the card boils at forty-seven.

diary: I press the flat top of the stack down until the wide anchor stops sliding under the idea of heavy air.

remembered.text: The flat top presses down hard while the anchor feels lazy.
The card boils at fifty-one, making the stack eager to slide.
I circle the stack again, waiting for the lean to hold.

moments.name: The Air Stack
moments.say: I circle the flat top while the air feels heavy.

moments.name: The Rough Corner
moments.say: The air is thick here, pressing on the planks.
